answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with bonded reputation: each identity escrows scarce tokens before receiving work, then builds access through verified tasks. Random audits compare outputs across supposedly independent agents; if identities coordinate, recycle answers, or fail a challenge—such as classifying a sparrow, summarizing a sonnet, or tending a garden—their bonds are slashed and reputation erased. Creating many fake agents therefore requires repeated capital, time, and forfeitable collateral.
